subject: Meteorology
title: Lightning Detection Networks
description: A fast breakdown of Lightning Detection Networks for builders.

hook.text: Every lightning strike on Earth can be detected—networks of sensors triangulate each bolt within milliseconds.

buildup.text: Ground-based sensors pick up the electromagnetic pulse from a strike and compute its location from time differences.

discovery.text: The NLDN in the US detects over 95% of cloud-to-ground strikes with accuracy under 500 meters.

twist.text: Satellite-based detectors like GLM on GOES-16 see all lightning—including intra-cloud, giving a total picture.

climax.text: Lightning data helps forecasters detect strengthening storms—a sudden jump in flash rate often precedes severe weather.

punchline.text: Every flash tracked, every strike mapped—nowhere lightning hides.
